text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Elf Aquitaine could disengage from its 53 percent pharmaceutical unit Sanofi to concentrate on core oil and chemicals activity, would favour a merger of Sanofi with another pharmaceutical laboratory to boost its profitability. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
LES ECHOS
-- German insurer Allianz says its interest in Credit Lyonnais after its restructuring would be limited to a less-than-ten-percent stake.
-- Dutch banking group ABN-Amro negotiates with Worms and Cie the acquisition of a majority stake in Banque Demachy Worms.
-- A planned merger between Dassault and Aerospatiale almost finalised.
-- State-controlled stake in computer maker Bull to fall under 49.2 percent after a second privatisation, as France Telecom, NEC and Motorola increase their stakes.
LA TRIBUNE

-- Former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing in an interview says that if the franc is overvalued when France shifts to a single currency, the French will have to "suffer twice", first to implement the change to euro, then to correct the effects of a possible overvalue. Repeats call for franc/dollar around 5.50 to 5.60 and says there is room in France to cut interest rates.
-- Thirty-seven percent of human resources heads expect labour unrest in the private sector in 1997, with higher wages coming first on the list of workers' demands, survey shows.
-- Insurer AGF buys stakes of BNP and Societe Generale in export insurance agency Coface.
-- OECD calls for a further easing of interest rates in France.
L'AGEFI
-- Preliminary bill on reforming corporate law to be studied by State Council.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Government softens decree stating that doctors ought to reimburse social security funds when they overshoot health spending targets.
-- Retail group Carrefour raises to 41.4 percent its stake in family-owned GMB holding controlling Cora supermarkets.
-- Merck and Rhone-Poulenc to merge animal health and poultry genetics businesses in a new 8.5-billion-franc-turnover company.
LIBERATION (Economic section)

-- Former German chancellor Helmut Schmidt says the strong mark policy implemented by the Bundesbank has fueled unemployment in Germany, adds he thinks Bundesbank governor Hans Tietmeyer and economist Otmar Issing are campaigning against a European single currency, says the mark and the franc are currently overvalued, calls for investment in research and development to fight unemployment in the future.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Elf authorizes Sanofi to look for partner.
